props.covers: Size follows content and communicates role: every node starts from one shared target rectangle, peers match the largest member, larger boxes signal importance, and off-target sizes signal exceptions; the capabilities roster keys no size to an object type.

text.insert: Size each box for what it says, then make peers match the largest member. Use a larger box only as a deliberate importance signal and an off-register size only as a deliberate exception.

Sizing starts from a stated target rather than from a blank page: a node aims for 288×96 and is never narrower than 224. That target belongs to every node equally — it is a rectangle to grow from, not a cap and not a lookup keyed by object type. Grow whichever dimension the label needs, then match peers to the largest member. What a box says decides its size; what kind of thing it is decides nothing.
defines content-first sizing and peer matching. The generated

lists bare type names, icon glyphs, and colors without default sizes, leaving every finite rectangle to the agent. The roster and the target do separate jobs: the roster refuses to attach a size to a type, and the target gives every node the same content-first place to start. Patched rectangles quantize to the 16px grid after the semantic size has been chosen. No diagnostic assigns an importance class or preferred extent.

Stickies have no documentation-level base size or override. Size a note for its markdown content and role, keep it inside the section it explains, and use the pushed render to judge readability. Short labels belong on objects; summaries, legends, callouts, explanations, and open questions belong on stickies.
